messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] Winbuilder issue on R API checks
messages.subject_clean: [R-pkg-devel] Winbuilder issue on R API checks
messages.body_plain:
I believe that there is an issue with Winbuilder failing the R API checks for compiled code.  I got a NOTE for a package submission:


* checking compiled code ... NOTE
Error in ccE(lines, flags = new_flags, include = include) :
  'cc' is not on the path
Calls: <Anonymous> ... lapply -> FUN -> lapply -> FUN -> getFunsHdr -> ccE
Execution halted


See 'Writing portable packages' in the 'Writing R Extensions' manual.
* checking installed files from 'inst/doc' ? OK

That seems to be coming from `cc` not being found in tools:::ccE() (src/library/tools/R/apitools.R) which invokes the C preprocessor as the literal command cc (via Sys.which("cc?))

Environment variable not being set?

As a check I uploaded an existing package on CRAN to Winbuilder and it ran into the same issue.

-Naras

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] windows devel builder down?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,


Is the windows R-devel builder (at win-builder.r-project.org) down?

I've uploaded the newest version of the 'broadcast' package to the windows R-devel for testing yesterday and the day before yesterday.
I have verified with 'foghorn::winbuilder_queue()' that my package was placed on the queue.
I've uploaded the package using 'devtools::check_win_devel()', and also tried uploading directly to the site (win-builder.r-project.org). In neither case have I received an e-mail, even after 24 hours.
I've also checked if the e-mail is correct in the Description file - it is.
I've tried accessing win-builder via an FTP client (File Zilla), to have a look at the folders, but the client is unable to connect to ftp://win-builder.r-project.org/, even after several attempts.
And of course, I've checked my e-mail's spam folder.

So, is there something wrong with the windows R-devel builder at win-builder.r-project.org?
If not, what could be the reason I'm not receiving e-mails?

(The R package itself is unlikely to have caused problems on the server, I think, as it passes all  R cmd checks on my laptop, on GitHUb actions (which includes windows platform), and on r-hub's valgrind checks.)

Kind regards,

Tony

Onderwerp: Re: [R-pkg-devel] windows devel builder down?

? Sat, 8 Aug 2026 08:49:50 +0000
Tony Wilkes <tony_a_wilkes at outlook.com> ?????:

> I've tried accessing win-builder via an FTP client (File Zilla), to
> have a look at the folders, but the client is unable to connect to
> ftp://win-builder.r-project.org/<ftp://win-builder.r-project.org/>, even after several attempts.

FileZilla stopped working with Win-Builder a few years ago. The server
doesn't seem to advertise EPSV support in reply to the FEAT command, so
FileZilla tries to use the standard passive mode ("PASV"), to which the
FTP server replies with an IP address that the client is unable to
reach. There are unanswered feature requests for EPSV support
preferences [*] in FileZilla.

Other clients (e.g. libcurl) work because they use the extended passive
mode ("EPSV") by default, without even asking for a list of features.
In reply to the EPSV command the FTP server gives an accessible port
number, and all works well.

--
Best regards,
Ivan

[*]
https://trac.filezilla-project.org/ticket/13100<https://trac.filezilla-project.org/ticket/13100>
https://trac.filezilla-project.org/ticket/10301<https://trac.filezilla-project.org/ticket/10301>

> does only provide amd64, but I do need arm64 to reproduce the

The problem here is that you're running an amd64 computer. If you
install QEMU (dnf install qemu-user-static), it should become possible
for you to run the container images on an emulated processor:

podman run --platform linux/arm64 ghcr.io/r-devel/rcheckserver/ubuntu

It will be very slow and may not reproduce the problem exactly, but
it's easier than shopping for a real 64-bit ARM machine to test on or
running everything remotely on GitHub Actions.

(QEMU did help me reproduce a problem on RISC-V a few months ago.)

-- 
Best regards,
Ivan

messages.subject: [R-pkg-devel] Docker image for "linux/arm64" ?
messages.body_plain:
rocker/r2u exists for the two newer Ubuntu releases 24.04 and 26.04 in both
the common 'amd64' and the newer 'arm64' variant.  (r-universe also has it.)

So besides working with the qemu emulator you could rely on GitHub Actions.
Create or fork a repo, and add an action based on the standard one proposed
by r-ci [1] but add one line in the 'matrix' containing

          - {os: ubuntu-latest}

to add one or both of

          - {os: ubuntu-26.04-arm}
          - {os: ubuntu-24.04-arm}

and your job will run on arm64 as well. As the rest of the action relies on
r2u, all your dependencies are taken care of.  I can set up a demo repo if
you prefer. If you find the 'matrix' confusing a simpler one-off is below [2]. 

As mentioned, you can rely on r-universe which builds on linux arm64 for you
to. No special setup from your side needed, but you have finer control for
your debugging via your own action.

Hope this helps, Dirk


[1] See http://eddelbuettel.github.io/r-ci
[2] Quick one-off yaml file to run R CMD check on arm for a give repo.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run CI for R using https://eddelbuettel.github.io/r-ci/

name: ci

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

env:
  _R_CHECK_FORCE_SUGGESTS_: "false"

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04-arm
    steps:
      
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout at v7
        
      - name: Setup
        uses: eddelbuettel/github-actions/r-ci at master
        
      - name: Dependencies
        run: ./run.sh install_all
        
      - name: Test
        run: ./run.sh run_tests
        
      - name: Logs
        run: ./run.sh dump_logs
        if: failure()
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------

-- 
dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org
